title: Flowise SQLite Record Manager -- T1059 additionalConfig spread overwrites the database path, planted content becomes a config-file RCE
author: WinstonRedGuard -- sigma plugin observed rules (derived from breach corpus)
description:
Vendor-disclosed detection for CVE-2026-69259, an elttam-disclosed
advisory affecting Flowise's SQLite Record Manager node.

`SQLiteRecordManager_RecordManager.init()` builds its TypeORM options
as `{ database, ...additionalConfiguration, type: 'sqlite' }` -- the
caller-controlled `additionalConfig` input is spread AFTER the
intended `database` path, so any key it sets (including `database`
itself) silently overwrites the preceding value. An attacker sets
`additionalConfig.database` to a system config path such as
`/etc/chromium/exploit.conf` (the Docker image runs as root) and, by
exploiting SQLite's binary record-length encoding to smuggle a `'`
character past the otherwise-safe `tableName` regex filter, writes a
crafted database file whose bytes, when later sourced by a Chromium
config-file reader (triggered when Puppeteer launches for an
unrelated Upsert Vector Store operation), execute a shell command via
argument injection -- confirmed end-to-end with a reverse shell as
root.

Detection logic flags a SQLite Record Manager node configuration
whose `additionalConfig` sets a `database` path outside the intended
Flowise data directory, particularly one targeting a system
configuration path such as `/etc/` -- the exact
spread-after-database override this advisory's reproduction uses to
redirect the SQLite file write.

Aggregated from 1 first-party vendor security advisory (elttam, via
a disclosed advisory citing the exact source file, the spread-order
root cause, a binary SQLite structure analysis, and a fully
reproduced reverse shell with `uid=0(root)` confirmation), fixed in Flowise 3.1.3 (verified via live GHSA lookup, 2026-09-04 -- the rule's original authoring predates the vendor's patch release; this note corrects a stale claim, not the detection logic itself).
